name: IN-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Yakym with large fundraising edge ($5.2M raised)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 4%
No polls or expert ratings; fundamentals dominate
model.rationale: Northern Indiana's R+13 lean, Yakym's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and markets pricing Democrats at roughly 4% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. Decio's modest war chest gives her little leverage in a district this red.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or a polling surprise showing Decio within single digits would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rudy Yakym, first elected in a 2022 special election, seeks another term in this heavily Republican northern Indiana district. The partisan lean of R+13, his incumbency advantage, and a fundraising gap of roughly $5.2 million raised to about $356,000 for Democrat Jamee Decio all favor the incumbent. Prediction markets give Decio only about a 4% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals. Decio has kept a modest cash reserve, but there is no outside spending or evidence of a competitive environment. A Libertarian candidate appears on the ballot but is not a significant factor. The seat remains safely in Republican hands.
